title: Boiled Egg Curry in Tomato Onion Masala
summary: A comforting Indian-style dinner of hard-boiled eggs simmered in a rich tomato and onion masala. It is warmly spiced, lightly tangy, and perfect with rice or flatbread.
steps: Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, then simmer for 9 minutes. Transfer to cold water, cool, peel, and lightly score each egg with shallow cuts so the sauce can cling to them.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and cook for 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until soft and deep golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger, and green chilli. Cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant and the raw smell has gone.
Stir in the cumin, ground coriander, turmeric, paprika, chilli powder, curry powder, and salt. Cook for 30 seconds, adding a splash of water if the spices start to catch.
Add the canned tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring regularly, until the masala thickens, darkens slightly, and the oil begins to separate at the edges.
Pour in the vegetable stock, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook for 5 minutes until the sauce is glossy and spoon-coating. Add a little more water if you prefer a looser curry.
Add the boiled eggs and simmer gently for 5 minutes, turning them once or twice to coat them in the masala.
Finish with chopped fresh coriander and serve hot with rice or flatbread.
